newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent seen up 15-20 cts, gas oil up $4.50 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent seen up 15-20 cts, gas oil up $4.50 a tonne.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures are expected to open firmer on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's robust rise on the back of supportive U.S. inventory data and technical strength, dealers said.

May Brent, which settled 75 cents higher at $20.25 a barrel, is expected to add 15-20 cents at the open while April gas oil should come in about $4.50 a tonne higher after settling at $172.00 a tonne.
"A technical break (on NYMEX) yesterday prompted a lot of fund buying, partly pre-empting the API figures and we should see a bit more this morning," said a broker.

Dealers said American Petoleum Institute (API) data for last week showing a nationwide build in crude stocks of just 76,000 barrels were well below market expectations, and a 4.3 million-barrel draw in gasoline inventories was also supportive.
Gasoline stocks, at 198 million barrels, were about 9.6 million barrels below levels at the same time last year, when a sharp spring rally ensued as the summer driving season approached.
But while dealers expected further gains early on Wednesday, they noted firm technical resistance on May Brent at $20.50 a barrel, Tuesday's session high.
"We're already seeing some light selling interest coming into Singapore," said a broker.
May Brent last traded on SIMEX at $20.42 a barrel, 17 cents up on the IPE close but two cents off an early Wednesday high.

A weak fundamental picture on northwest European spot markets, where late March cargoes of North Sea crude are struggling to find buyers, could act as a barrier to further substantial gains, dealers said.
U.N. approval for two more contracts under the Iraq oil-for-food deal, allowing an extra 2.6 million barrels in exports, was also bearish.
